children: faces a lower Wall Street price target ahead of earnings, with shares at $87.62, down approximately 5.74% from the previous close, at 12 pm ET Thursday. According to TheFly's report on TipRanks, Susquehanna cut its target to $105 from $115 while keeping a Neutral rating. That still leaves roughly 19.8% upside to the revised target. The valuation picture offers a sharper warning: shares stand 170.02% above the $32.45 GF Value estimate, suggesting the recovery already carries a hefty premium.

Intel's operating rebound gives investors something concrete to weigh. Its second-quarter release showed revenue of $16.1 billion, including $6.3 billion from Data Center and AI, up 59% year over year. Adjusted gross margin reached 41.8%. Those numbers strengthen the recovery case. The tougher question is how much more improvement the current valuation demands.

The next checkpoint arrives after the market closes on October 29, when Intel reports third-quarter results. Management's outlook calls for revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion and adjusted gross margin of 42%. That margin target represents just 20 basis points of sequential improvement. Investors have a clear test: can Intel turn stronger AI demand into sustained profit gains large enough to support its valuation?

title: Intel Stocks Fall 5.74% With a Lower Target Before October 29 Earnings
